record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.original_question: For the extreme Reissner–Nordström black hole in N = 2, d = 4 supergravity, the semiclassical Euclidean calculation gives entropy S = 0, while string state counting predicts S = πM² and the horizon-area interpretation of entropy also suggests a nonzero value. Which description gives the physically correct entropy of the extreme Reissner–Nordström black hole, and under what conditions does the semiclassical near-horizon geometry remain valid or break down at zero temperature?

evidence.quote: The B bound is M ≥ |Q + iP| = |Z|. The only static BH solution is RN's which depends on the ADM mass M, the electric charge Q and magnetic charge P. When the B bound is saturated and the SUSY limit is reached the extreme limit in which the two RN horizons coincide is also reached (extreme RN (ERN) solution).

However, Euclidean semiclassical calculations gave as result S = 0 for the ERN BH [14], in accordance with the conventional content of the third law of thermodynamics [15] and in open contrast with string state-counting results [16].

On the other hand one may always take the point of view that the geometry near the horizon is very different in the string picture [19] and the semiclassical approach breaks down there. In any case, the SUGRA result is S = 0, the string theory prediction is S = πM2 and we should regard his difference as a test (even if in gedanken experiments) for both theories.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the extreme Reissner–Nordström (ERN) black hole solution of four-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell theory embedded as the bosonic sector of N=2, d=4 supergravity. The metric depends on the ADM mass M and electric/magnetic charges (Q,P); the extreme limit is reached when the BPS bound M = |Z| = |Q+iP| is saturated and the two horizons of Reissner–Nordström coincide at r_H = M, giving horizon area A = 4πM².

Three different prescriptions assign an entropy to this black hole:
(i) The Euclidean semiclassical action computed by taking the extremal limit ab initio (with arbitrary period for Euclidean time, and topology distinct from the non-extreme case) yields S = 0, consistent with a strong form of the third law of thermodynamics.
(ii) Microscopic state counting of BPS states in string theory yields S = A/4 = πM².
(iii) The Bekenstein–Hawking area law applied directly to the extreme horizon also gives S = πM².

Problem. Determine which of these prescriptions assigns the physically correct thermodynamic entropy to the extreme Reissner–Nordström black hole, and characterize precisely the conditions (in terms of the near-horizon geometry, Euclidean topology, choice of ensemble, and the limit T→0 of the temperature) under which the semiclassical Euclidean derivation that yields S = 0 is valid, and the conditions under which it breaks down so that the area-law / microscopic value S = πM² is recovered. In particular, decide whether the discrepancy reflects a genuine breakdown of the semiclassical near-horizon description at zero temperature or merely an inequivalent choice of boundary conditions in the path integral.
artifact.status_search_result: The discrepancy has been clarified but is not universally regarded as fully settled. String-theoretic BPS state counting (Strominger–Vafa and successors) supports S = A/4 = πM² for extremal charged black holes, and this is now the widely accepted physical value. The S = 0 result of the Euclidean semiclassical computation has been attributed to subtleties of the extremal topology (arbitrary Euclidean time periodicity, distinct topology from the non-extreme case) and to taking the extremal limit before quantization; recent works (e.g., 2505.16309) re-examine the nonextremal-to-extremal limit and recover the area law. Conceptual analyses (e.g., 1904.03232) continue to debate whether the semiclassical near-horizon description genuinely breaks down at T = 0.

status_evidence.title: From Nonextremal to Extremal: Entropy of Reissner-Nordström and Kerr black holes Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Re-examines the limit from nonextremal to extremal RN/Kerr and the resulting entropy, recovering the area law in the extremal limit.
status_evidence.claim: Recent re-analysis supports S = A/4 in the extremal limit, reconciling with string-counting results.

status_evidence.title: Conceptual Analysis of Black Hole Entropy in String Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the tension between zero gravitational entropy for ERN from Euclidean methods and the non-zero entropy from string-theoretic state counting, and discusses how the resolution depends on framework.
status_evidence.claim: The discrepancy is framework-dependent; string counting yields S = A/4 while the naive Euclidean prescription can yield S = 0.

status_evidence.title: Entropy for extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Original discussion of the S = 0 Euclidean result for extreme RN.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the semiclassical computation giving S = 0 that contrasts with area-law and microscopic results.
